AccessRequest.description: One HCP authorization detail as requested (HCP 6.1.5, 13.3).

actions.description: HCP `actions`: what the client may do with the categories. `provenance` only alongside `read` (HCP 6.1.5, 7.4.1).

categories.description: HCP `categories` the detail covers (HCP 4.5, 6.1.5). The maxItems of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

narrowedTo.description: HCP `narrowedTo` (HCP 6.1.5.1): implementation-defined keys that only narrow. A key the provider does not support is refused with malformedRequest (HCP 6.1.5.1 rule 2).

onwardSharing.description: HCP `onwardSharing` (HCP 3.12, 6.1.4, 6.1.5): asks that the person be offered onward sharing for this detail, as a separate act after they confirm the grant. Only in a detail that includes `read` and whose categories are all of Low default sensitivity; otherwise malformedRequest (HCP 6.1.5).

purposes.description: HCP `purposes` the client asks to use the categories for (HCP 6.1.5.2). Absent means the person chooses them before approving (HCP 6.1.5.2, 13.3). The maxItems of 32 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

Category.description: An HCP context category (HCP 4.5), the primary unit of access control: either a slug from HCP's category registry, such as `general_preferences` or `health_context`, or a custom category written as an absolute URI under a domain its definer controls. A custom category is not portable between providers without bilateral agreement (HCP 4.5).

GrantAction.description: An HCP grant action (HCP 6.1.5). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

GrantedAccess.description: One authorization detail as the person approved it (HCP 6.1.5 `access[]`). Every approved detail carries at least one purpose (HCP 6.1.5.2).

categories.description: HCP `categories` as approved (HCP 6.1.5); may be fewer than asked.

narrowedTo.description: HCP `narrowedTo`, present wherever the grant is narrowed (HCP 6.1.5.1 rule 3).

onwardSharing.description: HCP `onwardSharing`, present only where the person elected it (HCP 6.1.4, 6.1.5), with `domains` and the provider-set `notTo` as HCP defines them.

purposes.description: HCP `purposes` as approved (HCP 6.1.5.2): the purposes a query under this grant may name.

OnwardSharingRequest.description: A request for onward sharing (HCP 6.1.5). `notTo` is set by the provider, never asked for.

domains.description: DNS domains the client proposes to limit onward sharing to. The person may narrow them further (HCP 6.1.4).

Purpose.description: An HCP purpose (HCP 6.1.5.2): a code and a description the person can read.

description.description: What the purpose means, in words the person can read. The provider shows its own description where it has one. The maxLength is a framework bound.

PurposeCode.description: An HCP purpose code: an absolute URI naming the purpose for which context is requested or may be used (HCP 6.1.5.2).

id.description: HCP `requestingParty.id`: an identifier for the party.

name.description: HCP `requestingParty.name`: a name the person can recognize, shown before they act (HCP 6.1.6).

Response.description: The person approved: the grant evidence and the grant as approved. Sent only after the person's affirmative act (HCP 6.1.6); while they decide the provider answers trust-task-next-step, and a decline is trust-task-error permissionDenied — never this shape.

access.description: HCP `access` as the person approved it, which may be narrower than asked (HCP 6.1.5, 13.3: the token response carries the authorization details granted).

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the new grant, opaque to the client. The client presents it unchanged as `accessToken` in hcp/entries/query and every other hcp/* task it sends under the grant. Its lifetime follows HCP 13.4 (default 1 hour, at most 24 hours).

grantExpiresAt.description: HCP grant `expiresAt` (HCP 6.1.3, 6.1.4): REQUIRED for a temporary grant, and absent for a persistent one, where HCP writes null.

grantId.description: HCP `grantId` (HCP 6.1.5): stable for the life of the grant, and the identifier hcp/grants/revoke and hcp/grants/revoked name.

grantType.description: HCP `grantType` as the person chose it (HCP 6.1.4).

grantedAt.description: HCP grant `issuedAt` (HCP 6.1.5), renamed so it is not read as the document's own `issuedAt`.

tokenExpiresAt.description: When `accessToken` stops being accepted (HCP 13.4), in whole seconds. Never after `grantExpiresAt`.

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

schema.description: A Context Client asks an HCP Provider for a grant over a person's context, naming what it needs as HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5; RFC 9396 `authorization_details` of the HCP type, as HCP 13.3 names them). HCP Core defines no grant-request operation (HCP 6.1.7 leaves it to the profiles), so this task carries no HCP operation: it is a Trust-Task-native authenticated channel in the sense of HCP 6.1.6 and 12.2. The person decides out of band; while they do, the provider answers with trust-task-next-step. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3.

access.description: What the client asks to be granted: one or more HCP authorization details (HCP 6.1.5 `access`, HCP 13.3). The provider shows each to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6). The maxItems of 16 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

expiresIn.description: For a temporary grant, the lifetime the client asks for, in seconds. Absent means HCP's default of 4 hours; HCP's maximum is 24 hours (HCP 6.1.3). The provider MAY grant less and never more. Ignored for a persistent grant.

grantType.description: The kind of grant the client asks for (HCP 6.1.4). Absent means `temporary`, HCP's default. `persistent` only lets the person be offered persistence as a separate affirmative act; it never pre-selects it (HCP 6.1.4), and the grant is temporary unless the person elects otherwise. Pending HCP confirmation.

requestingParty.description: HCP `requestingParty` (HCP 3.4, 6.1.5): the person or organization on whose behalf the client asks, where it differs from the Context Subject. Shown to the person before they act (HCP 6.1.6).

subjectHint.description: An identifier by which the provider can find the person whose context is asked for, and reach them to decide — the counterpart of OpenID Connect `login_hint`. Absent where the provider serves one person only. The provider never says whether it knows the hint (see the specification's Errors). Pending HCP confirmation.
